history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration strengthen measures for reducing the early turnover of resident coordinators to ensure the effective performance of the resident coordinator system.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers the recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure. There is no official definition of early turnover, and each of the alleged cases of early turnover are attributable to one of the three causes enumerated below, all of which are legitimate. The Administration respectfully points out that all the alleged cases of early turnover are provided for in the normative framework of the Organization and are therefore legitimate. The Administration cannot be held accountable for practices that fall squarely within its normative framework. 1. The fact that resident coordinators leave their positions during the last year of their tour of duty is fully in accordance with administrative instruction ST/AI/2022/1 on resident coordinator selection. See paragraph 4.8: “Currently serving resident coordinators are normally eligible to apply if, by the position start date, they have one year or less of service remaining in their current tour of duty.” 2. When early departure is due to early retirement or resignation, the Development Coordination Office cannot be held accountable, given that such departures are attributable to the individual decisions of staff members. 3. It is within the rights of the Organization to move resident coordinators prematurely for operational reasons and/or exigencies of service. This ensures that the right resident coordinator is in the right location at the right time, as expected by Member States.
history.board_assessment: In 2024, among the 130 established resident coordinator positions, there were 28 separations that occurred before the end of the resident coordinator’s term. While the Administration had provided explanations for these premature departures, the persistently high turnover rate in 2024 continued to impair the resident coordinator system’s capacity to effectively deliver its mandate at the country level. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration strengthen measures for reducing the early turnover of resident coordinators to ensure the effective performance of the resident coordinator system.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Administration notes that the instances referred to as “early turnover” are addressed in the Organization’s established regulatory framework, specifically the administrative instruction on resident coordinator selection (ST/AI/2022/1). As such, these instances fall within the scope of approved norms, and the Administration’s actions are in full compliance with the provisions of ST/AI/2022/01.
history.board_assessment: The early turnover of resident coordinators was reduced in 2025. Among the 130 established resident coordinator positions, there were 9 resident coordinators whose appointment or term was shortened due to reassignment, retirement or other factors. The Board therefore considers the recommendation to be implemented.
